questions.question: James Augustus Hickey is also known as father of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Journalism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• James Augustus Hicky was an Irishman who launched the first printed newspaper in India, Hickey's Bengal Gazette.
 
• The Bombay Samachar, now Mumbai Samachar, is the oldest continuously published newspaper in India established in 1822 by Fardunjee Marzban, it is published in Gujarati and English. 
 
• The Lahore Chronicle was started by Syed Muhammad Azim, father of the Punjab historian, in 1849.

 
• Hickeys Bengal Gazette or the Original Calcutta General Advertiser was an English language weekly newspaper published in Kolkata (then Calcutta), the capital of British India.
 
• It was the first newspaper printed in Asia and was published for two years, between 1780 and 1782, before the East India Company seized the newspaper's types and printing press.
 
• Founded by James Augustus Hickey a highly eccentric Irishman who had previously spent two years in jail for debt, the newspaper was a strong critic of the administration of Governor-General Warren Hastings. 
 
• The newspaper was important for its provocative journalism and its fight for free expression in India.
 
• Hickey first maintained a neutral editing policy (his slogan was "Open to all Parties, but Influenced by None") but after he learned that competitors with ties to the East India Company were intending to launch a rival newspaper, the India Gazette, he changed his editorial stance.
 
• Hickey accused an East India Company employee, Simeon Droz, of supporting the India Gazette as punishment for Hickey's refusal to pay a bribe to Droz and Marian Hastings, Warren Hastings' wife.
 
• Hickey claimed Hastings' order violated his right to free expression and accused Hastings of corruption, tyranny.
 
• Hickey also accused other British leaders in Calcutta of corruption, including the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, Elijah Impey of taking bribes, and the leader of the Protestant Mission, Johann Zacharias Kiernander of stealing from an orphaned children's fund.
 
• Hickey's editorial independence was short-lived as Hastings and Kiernander sued him for libel. After four dramatic trials in June 1781, the Supreme Court found Hickey guilty and sentenced him to jail.
 
• Hickey continued to print his newspaper from jail and continued to accuse Hastings and others of corruption.

questions.question: The first Indian to win the All England Badminton Championship in 1980 ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakash Padukone**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prakash Padukone became the **first Indian to win the prestigious All England Badminton Championship in 1980.**
 
• Prakash Padukone defeated Indonesia's Liem Swie King, a top player of that era, in the** final with a score of 15–3, 15–10.**
 
• Along with the All England title, Padukone won many other international titles and became a trailblazer for Indian badminton players worldwide.
 
• He was honored with the **Arjuna Award in 1972**, recognizing his excellence and contribution to Indian sports, particularly badminton.
 
• **In 1982, Prakash Padukone received the Padma Shri,** India's fourth-highest civilian award, for his outstanding achievements in badminton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kiran Bedi**

 
 
• Kiran Bedi became the **first woman to join the Indian Police Service (IPS) in 1972**, breaking gender barriers in law enforcement.
 
• She was awarded the **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Government Service in 1994** for her pioneering reforms in the Indian prison system, particularly at Tihar Jail.
 
• She was Inspector General of Tihar Jail, she introduced several innovative reforms focused on education, meditation, and rehabilitation for inmates.
 
• Kiran Bedi served as the **Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry** from 2016 to 2021, contributing to the administration and governance of the Union Territory.
 
 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar**
 
 
• Sachin Tendulkar is the only cricketer in the world to **score 100 international centuries (51 in Test cricket and 49 in One-Day Internationals).**
 
• He was at the age of 17, Tendulkar became the youngest Indian to score a Test century, achieving this milestone against England at Old Trafford in 1990.
 
• In 2010, Tendulkar became the **first player in history to score a double century in a One-Day International**, against South Africa.
 
• He was **awarded the Bharat Ratna,** India's highest civilian honor, in 2014, becoming the first sportsperson to receive this recognition.
 
 
 
• **Dhyan Chand**
 
 
• Dhyan Chand earned the nickname **"The Wizard"** for his extraordinary ball control and dribbling abilities on the hockey field.
 
• He won **three Olympic gold medals** in field hockey for India in** 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles), and 1936 (Berlin).**
 
• Dhyan Chand is regarded as one of the greatest field hockey players in history, known for his exceptional goal-scoring skills.
 
• His birthday, **August 29, is celebrated as National Sports Day** in India, honoring his contributions to Indian sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other famous Indian badminton players:**

 
 
• **Pullela Gopichand**

 
 
• He won the All England Badminton Championship in 2001, becoming the second Indian to achieve this feat after Prakash Padukone.
 
 
 
• **Saina Nehwal**
 
 
• Saina Nehwal became the **first Indian badminton player to win an Olympic medal **(bronze) at the 2012 London Olympics and has held the world No. 1 ranking in women's singles.
 
 
 
• **P.V. Sindhu**:
 
 
• P.V. Sindhu won a **silver medal **at the 2016 Rio Olympics, a** bronze **at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, and became the first Indian to win the BWF World Championships (gold in 2019).
 
 
 
• **Kidambi Srikanth**
 
 
• Kidambi Srikanth became the **first Indian male badminton player to win four Super Series **titles in a calendar year (2017), and he achieved the world No. 1 ranking in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Lakshya Sen**
 
 
• A rising star in Indian badminton, **Lakshya Sen won the bronze medal at the 2021 BWF World Championships** and the gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

questions.question: When calculating Net National Product (NNP), what is deducted from Gross National Product (GNP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Depreciation**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP) **measures the total value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents within a specific time period, including income earned by residents from investments abroad.
 
• Depreciation accounts for the reduction in value of capital goods over time due to wear and tear or obsolescence.
 
• By subtracting **depreciation from GNP, you arrive at Net National Product (NNP),** which reflects the actual value of goods and services produced, taking into account the loss of value in capital assets.
 
• The formula can be summarized as:** NNP=GNP−Depreciation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsidies**

 
 
• Subsidies are government financial assistance provided to individuals or businesses to **promote economic activity **and** reduce costs**.
 
• They include direct cash payments, tax breaks, price supports, and grants.
 
• Subsidies can stimulate growth and lower consumer prices but may also cause market distortions and strain government budgets.
 
• Common examples include** agricultural subsidies, energy subsidies for renewables**, and education subsidies for higher education.
 
 
 
• **Indirect taxes**
 
 
• Indirect taxes are taxes levied on goods and services rather than on income or profits, meaning they are **not directly paid by the individual but are passed on through the price of goods.**
 
• Common forms of indirect taxes include sales tax,** value-added tax (VAT),** excise duty, and customs duty.
 
• Indirect taxes increase the cost of goods and services, which can lead to higher prices for consumers, making them less visible than direct taxes.
 
• Indirect taxes are a significant **source of revenue for governments**, as they are easier to collect and can be applied to a wide range of products and services.
 
 
 
• **Personal income**
 
 
• Personal income refers to the **total earnings received by an individual from various sources,** including wages, salaries, investments, rental income, and government benefits.
 
• It includes wages, bonuses, interest income, dividends, rents, and any other forms of **earnings before taxes are deducted.**
 
• Personal income is a **key indicator of an individual's economic** health and purchasing power, influencing consumption, savings, and overall economic activity.
 
• Personal income is subject to income tax, which varies based on the individual's income level and applicable tax laws in their country or region.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to become a member of Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 80** of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age to become a member of the **Rajya Sabha is 30 years.**
 
• The Rajya Sabha is composed of a **maximum of 250 members,** of which **238 are elected by the Legislative Assemblies** of the States and Union territories, and **12 are appointed by the President **of India.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha serve a term of six years, with **one-third of the members retiring every two years**, ensuring continuity in the house.
 
• Besides age, candidates must be citizens of India and should not be disqualified under any law made by Parliament, as outlined in **Article 84 of the Constitution.**
 
• The Rajya Sabha plays a crucial role in representing the states and union territories at the national level, contributing to the legislative process, and reviewing legislation passed by the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lok Sabha**

 
 
• The minimum age to become a member of the **Lok Sabha is 25 years**, as per **Article 84 **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Lok Sabha consists of 545 members, with 543 elected by the public and 2 appointed by the President (though the latter provision has been abolished).
 
• Members serve a term of** five years,** unless the house is dissolved earlier.
 
• Candidates must be Indian citizens and not disqualified under any law, as specified in **Article 102.**
 
 
 
• **President and Vice President**
 
 
• According to **Article 58** of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age to become the President of India is** 35 years.**
 
• To be eligible for the presidency, a** candidate must be a citizen of India**, he candidate must be eligible to be a member of either the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha, and must not hold any office of profit under the Government, as stated in Article 58.
 
• As per** Article 66, the minimum age to become the Vice President of India is also 35 years**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Panchayat (local self-government) in India**:

 
 
• The minimum age to contest in** Panchayat elections is 21 years**, as specified in **Article 243F** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system is a three-tier system of local self-government in rural areas, consisting of the **Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).**
 
• The specific rules and regulations governing Panchayat elections, including age and eligibility criteria, may vary slightly from** state to state, **as each state has the authority to enact its own Panchayat laws.

questions.question: How many major theories have been established on the origin of iron in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indigenous Origin Theory**

 
 
• This theory suggests that **iron smelting and production developed independently in India **based on early evidence of iron use in various regions of the country.
 
• Notably, iron artifacts dating back to **around 1000 BCE **have been discovered in southern India.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion Theory**
 
 
• This theory posits that iron technology was introduced to India through cultural diffusion from the Near **East or Central Asia,** likely via trade or migration.
 
• It suggests that iron smelting knowledge spread across regions, arriving in India during the **second millennium BCE.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact on Society**

 
 
• The introduction and independent development of** iron technology** significantly transformed ancient Indian society, contributing to advancements in agriculture (with iron plows), warfare (with iron weapons), and overall economic development.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Evidence**
 
 
• Sites like** Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh** also reveal extensive use of iron, showcasing its importance in various cultural and technological contexts throughout ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• The transition from the **Bronze Age to the Iron Age** marked a crucial turning point in Indian history, leading to the rise of urbanization and complex societies. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bronze **was prominently used during the** Indus Valley Civilization (around 3300–1300 BCE),** which is one of the earliest urban cultures in India.
 
• The civilization showcased advanced metallurgy techniques, including the **casting of bronze.**
 
• Various bronze artifacts, including tools, weapons, and decorative items, have been discovered at archaeological sites such as **Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa**.
 
• These items indicate the sophisticated level of craftsmanship and metalworking skills in ancient Indian society.
 
• The transition from the** Bronze Age to the Iron Age** in India marked a significant shift in technology and society.
 
• While bronze was essential for** various tools and weapons**, the advent of** iron metallurgy around 1000 BCE** led to advancements in agriculture, warfare, and trade.

• The** National Dental Commission Bill, 2023** aims to establish a national framework for the regulation of dental education and practice in India.
 
• The Bill proposes the establishment of the **National Dental Commission (NDC)**, which will be responsible for formulating policies for dental education and practice, as well as maintaining a registry of dental professionals in India.
 
• The **NDC will regulate dental colleges,** set educational standards, and accredit dental institutions.
 
• It aligns with the Ministry's broader goals to enhance healthcare delivery by integrating dental care into overall health policies.

• The Finance Ministry formulates and implements financial policies, **manages the economic framework**, and oversees the national **budget, taxation, and public expenditure.**
 
• It prepares the annual Union Budget, detailing government spending and revenue plans, and presents it in Parliament to ensure** fiscal discipline.**
 
• The ministry develops **economic policies aimed **at promoting sustainable growth, managing inflation, and ensuring financial stability.
 
• It comprises several departments, including the Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Revenue, Department of Expenditure, and Department of Financial Services, each handling specific aspects of financial governance .
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**
 
 
• The Ministry is responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to **international and domestic trade** to promote exports and manage imports.
 
• It plays a crucial role in boosting industrial growth, supporting businesses, and fostering investment opportunities to enhance **economic development**.
 
• The Ministry works to improve the ease of doing business by simplifying regulations, encouraging **foreign direct investment (FDI),** and promoting entrepreneurship.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**
 
 
• Formulates policies for **social justice** for marginalized groups, including **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.**
 
• Focuses on empowering **women, children, and persons with disabilities** through various schemes for equal opportunities.
 
• Oversees programs to improve living standards of vulnerable populations, providing financial assistance and skill development.
 
• Develops and implements laws like the** Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act** to ensure protection and rights for marginalized communities.

questions.question: As of 2023, when was the last fundamental duty added to Article 51 A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2002.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The last Fundamental Duty was added to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution by the** 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002.**
 
• This amendment inserted** Clause (k),** which states: "It shall be the duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years."
 
• This duty was added to complement the** Right to Education**, which became a fundamental right under** Article 21A **through the same amendment, ensuring free and compulsory education for children in this age group.
 
• It **strengthens the Directive Principles of State Policy** by creating a legal obligation for parents to ensure their children receive an education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Article 51A (b)

 Article 51A (c)
 To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
 

 Article 51A (d)

 Article 51A (e)

 Article 51A (f)

 To provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 and 14 years (for parents/guardians).
